scenarios.name: Hero Section Display
scenarios.description: Verify the hero section displays product name, tagline, value proposition, and call-to-action buttons correctly

steps.description: Navigate to the MirDB homepage in a browser
steps.context: Fresh page load with cleared cache

steps.description: Check that product name 'MirDB', tagline, and description are visible within first viewport
steps.context: Hero section should be above the fold

steps.description: Confirm 'Get Started' and 'View on GitHub' buttons are present and visible

test_cases.input: Load index.html and check for product name element
test_cases.expected: Element containing 'MirDB' text is present and visible in hero section
Tagline containing 'Persistent Key-Value Store' and 'Memcached Protocol' is displayed
'Get Started' button is visible and has appropriate styling
'View on GitHub' or 'GitHub' button is visible with link to repository

scenarios.name: Features Section Display
scenarios.description: Verify the features section presents key capabilities with appropriate descriptions

steps.description: Scroll to or locate the features section on the homepage
steps.context: Features section should be below hero

steps.description: Check that all key features are displayed with titles and descriptions
steps.context: Should include Memcached compatibility, persistence, LSM-tree, and configuration features

test_cases.expected: Feature card/section for 'Memcached Compatible' with description about client compatibility
Feature card/section for 'Persistent Storage' or 'Built-in Persistence' with SSTables mention
Feature card/section for 'LSM-Tree' architecture with write optimization description
Feature card/section for 'Configuration' with TOML mention
Features are displayed in grid or card layout with consistent styling

scenarios.name: Code Example Section
scenarios.description: Verify code examples section displays syntax-highlighted, readable code demonstrating basic MirDB operations

steps.description: Scroll to or locate the code examples section
Check that code examples show server startup and basic memcached operations
Confirm code blocks have syntax highlighting applied

test_cases.input: Check for code block element with syntax highlighting
test_cases.expected: Pre/code elements with syntax highlighting classes (e.g., language-bash, language-shell)

test_cases.input: Verify MirDB server start command in examples
test_cases.expected: Code example includes command like 'mirdb -c' for starting the server
Code example includes 'set' command with sample key-value
Code example includes 'get' command demonstrating value retrieval

test_cases.input: Check code readability on different screen sizes
test_cases.expected: Code blocks are readable with horizontal scroll if needed on mobile

scenarios.name: Architecture Section
scenarios.description: Verify architecture section displays visual diagram and explanation of MirDB internals

steps.description: Scroll to or locate the architecture section
steps.context: Section should explain LSM-tree and data flow

steps.description: Check for visual diagram showing data flow architecture
steps.context: Should show WAL, Memtable, SSTable relationship

steps.description: Confirm brief explanation of LSM-tree benefits is present

test_cases.input: Check for architecture diagram image or SVG
test_cases.expected: Visual diagram element (img, svg, or canvas) showing data flow is present

test_cases.input: Verify diagram has alt text for accessibility
test_cases.expected: Architecture diagram has descriptive alt text
Text explaining LSM-tree structure and benefits is present
Content mentions WAL, Memtable, SSTable, and compaction

scenarios.name: Getting Started Section
scenarios.description: Verify getting started section provides installation and configuration guidance

steps.description: Scroll to or locate the getting started section
steps.context: Section should help users begin using MirDB

steps.description: Check for installation command or instructions
Check for TOML configuration example

test_cases.expected: Installation instructions or command is present and visible
TOML configuration example with key parameters is displayed
Link to full documentation is present and functional
Default values (port 12333, work directory, etc.) are shown

scenarios.name: Navigation and Links
scenarios.description: Verify all navigation elements and external links function correctly

steps.description: Locate all buttons, links, and navigation items on the page
steps.context: Include header, footer, and inline links

steps.description: Click each link and verify it navigates to correct destination
steps.context: External links should open valid pages

test_cases.expected: Button navigates to getting started section or documentation
Link opens GitHub repository page

test_cases.input: Verify all href attributes are valid
test_cases.expected: No broken links (404 errors) on the page

test_cases.input: Test anchor links for section navigation
test_cases.expected: Anchor links scroll to correct sections smoothly

scenarios.name: Footer Section
scenarios.description: Verify footer contains required project links and information

steps.description: Scroll to the bottom of the page to view footer
steps.context: Footer should be at page bottom

steps.description: Check for GitHub link, license info, and version/status

test_cases.expected: Footer element is present at bottom of page

test_cases.input: Verify GitHub repository link in footer
test_cases.expected: Footer contains link to GitHub repository
License information or link is displayed
Version or status information is visible

scenarios.name: Responsive Design - Mobile
scenarios.description: Verify homepage renders correctly on mobile devices (320px-768px viewport)

steps.description: Resize browser or use mobile device simulation at 375px width
Check all sections render properly without horizontal overflow
Verify buttons and links have adequate touch target size

test_cases.expected: All content visible without horizontal scrolling (except code blocks)
Layout adapts properly, text remains readable
All interactive elements are at least 44x44px
Navigation elements are accessible and functional on mobile
Feature cards stack vertically and remain readable

scenarios.name: Responsive Design - Tablet
scenarios.description: Verify homepage renders correctly on tablet devices (768px-1024px viewport)

steps.description: Resize browser to 768px width (iPad portrait)
Check layout adapts appropriately for medium screens

test_cases.expected: Layout transitions appropriately from mobile to tablet view
Layout uses available space effectively, may show grid layouts

test_cases.input: Verify feature grid layout on tablet
test_cases.expected: Feature cards display in 2-column grid or appropriate layout

scenarios.name: Responsive Design - Desktop
scenarios.description: Verify homepage renders correctly on desktop screens (1024px+ viewport)

steps.description: Use 1920px viewport width for standard desktop
Check all sections use desktop layout with full features

test_cases.expected: Full desktop layout with proper spacing and alignment
Layout scales appropriately for large screens, max-width constraints applied
Feature cards display in 3-4 column grid layout

scenarios.name: Cross-Browser Compatibility
scenarios.description: Verify homepage renders correctly across modern browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)

steps.description: Load homepage in Google Chrome and verify all functionality
Load homepage in Mozilla Firefox and verify all functionality
Load homepage in Safari and verify all functionality
Load homepage in Microsoft Edge and verify all functionality

test_cases.expected: All elements render correctly, no console errors, links work
All elements render correctly, no console errors, links work
All elements render correctly, no console errors, links work
All elements render correctly, no console errors, links work

scenarios.name: Page Performance
scenarios.description: Verify homepage loads within acceptable performance thresholds

steps.description: Load homepage and measure time to interactive
Execute Lighthouse performance audit
Verify CSS, JS, and image sizes are optimized

test_cases.input: Measure page load time on broadband
test_cases.expected: Page fully loads in under 3 seconds
Lighthouse performance score is 90 or above
Total page size is reasonable for static site (<1MB uncompressed)
Critical CSS inlined or async loading for JS

scenarios.name: Accessibility - Keyboard Navigation
scenarios.description: Verify page is fully navigable using keyboard only

steps.description: Use Tab key to navigate through all interactive elements
Check that focused elements have visible focus styles
Verify buttons and links can be activated with keyboard

test_cases.expected: All interactive elements receive focus in logical order
Focused elements have visible focus indicator (outline or highlight)
Buttons can be activated with Enter key when focused
Links can be activated with Enter key when focused

scenarios.name: Accessibility - Semantic HTML
scenarios.description: Verify page uses semantic HTML structure for accessibility

steps.description: Review HTML source for semantic elements
steps.context: header, nav, main, section, footer elements

steps.description: Verify headings follow logical h1-h6 hierarchy

test_cases.expected: Page uses header, main, footer, section, and nav elements appropriately
Single h1 element, headings follow sequential order (no skipping levels)
Main content area has appropriate ARIA landmarks if needed
Interactive actions use button elements, not styled divs/spans

scenarios.name: Accessibility - Images and Alt Text
scenarios.description: Verify all images have appropriate alt text

steps.description: Locate all img elements and background images with semantic meaning
Check each image has descriptive alt text
steps.context: Alt text should describe image content

test_cases.input: Check all img elements for alt attribute
test_cases.expected: All img elements have alt attribute with descriptive text
Architecture diagram has alt text describing the data flow
Purely decorative images have empty alt='' attribute

scenarios.name: Accessibility - Color Contrast
scenarios.description: Verify sufficient color contrast for all text content

steps.description: Verify all text has sufficient contrast ratio against background
steps.context: WCAG 2.1 AA requires 4.5:1 for normal text

steps.description: Verify buttons and links meet contrast requirements

test_cases.expected: All text meets WCAG 2.1 AA contrast requirements (4.5:1 normal, 3:1 large)
Code blocks have sufficient contrast for syntax highlighted text
Links are distinguishable from regular text (underline or color)

scenarios.name: Static Hosting Compatibility
scenarios.description: Verify the homepage can be deployed as static files without server-side processing

steps.description: List all files required for the homepage
Confirm all functionality works without server-side code

test_cases.input: Serve files from simple HTTP server
test_cases.expected: Page renders correctly from any static file server
No PHP, Node.js, or other server-side code required

test_cases.input: Verify all assets use relative paths
test_cases.expected: All asset references work regardless of deployment path
Page functions when opened as file:// (with CORS considerations)

scenarios.name: Error Handling - Missing Assets
scenarios.description: Verify page handles missing or failed asset loads gracefully

steps.description: Block CSS file and verify page remains usable
Block JavaScript and verify core content displays
Block images and verify alt text appears

test_cases.expected: Content remains readable and accessible without styling
Core content and navigation work without JS (syntax highlighting may be missing)
Alt text displays for all images, layout remains intact
